page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7a.8xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance powered by the x86_64 AMD EPYC 7T83 processor. The instance provides 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at a base clock frequency of 2.55 GHz. Memory capacity is configured at 64.0 GB, yielding a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage and lacks hardware GPU acceleration, requiring network-attached storage for persistent storage operations. Network connectivity is rated at a baseline bandwidth of 8 Gbps over a KVM hypervisor architecture.

Benchmark assessments indicate strong single-core computational execution, highlighted by a top-quartile stress-ng single-core rating and elevated scores in lightweight LLM text generation. Overall multi-core throughput, including Geekbench multi-threaded metrics and clang software compilation, resides squarely in the median bracket across comparable instances. Evaluated memory performance shows strong PassMark memory benchmark results alongside standard read speeds, though uncached write operations register in the lower quartile at 18.87 GB/sec.

In terms of qualitative efficiency, the instance provides high thread density for workloads requiring consistent processor allocation without incurring the cost of excess memory overhead. The primary hardware tradeoff lies in the absence of onboard NVMe storage and subdued uncached write bandwidth, placing dependency on external storage performance. The configuration is appropriate for distributed batch processing, web application hosting, continuous integration and build pipelines, and compute-focused backend API services.

It includes 64.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio, and operates over an 8 Gbps baseline network link. The server contains no local storage and no GPU acceleration, necessitating external block storage for persistent operational state. Performance benchmarks demonstrate strong single-core CPU throughput and responsive light model token generation, alongside median multi-core and software compilation capabilities. Memory read rates and synthetic memory indexing remain solid, balanced against lower uncached memory write bandwidth. Delivering high processing core density without the cost profile of large memory pools, this instance is suited for compute-intensive batch jobs, continuous integration pipelines, and high-concurrency web serving workloads.
